questions.prompt: Which expression is required in every @for block?
questions.explanation: track is mandatory in @for — the template won't compile without it. It gives each item a stable identity for efficient DOM reuse.

questions.prompt: Do you need to import CommonModule to use @if, @for, and @switch?

options.text: No — they are built into the template compiler

questions.explanation: Built-in control flow is part of the compiler, so no CommonModule import is needed.

questions.prompt: What operator does @switch use to match a @case, and does it fall through?
questions.explanation: @switch matches with strict === and never falls through, so no break is needed.

questions.prompt: Which contextual variables are available inside an @for block? (Select all that apply.)
Which optional @for block renders when the collection has zero items?
questions.explanation: @empty gives lists a friendly, intentional empty state.

options.text: Always — it is the most efficient option
Only for static lists that never reorder or change
Only when the list has unique ids
Never — $index cannot be used for track

questions.explanation: For dynamic lists, track by a stable unique property like id; $index can cause Angular to reuse the wrong DOM nodes.
